title: A Fish Does a Headstand to Tell an Eel Where Dinner Is Hiding
subject: coral grouper

scenes.text: A fish does a headstand to point at its dinner.
It's a roving coral grouper, and it's fast in open water.
But prey hides in cracks. The grouper can't reach in. A giant moray eel can.
So the grouper swims up to the eel and shakes its head in its face. It means: hunt with me.
Then it points. A headstand over the hiding spot shows the eel exactly where to go.
Scientists call it pointing, a skill once linked mostly to apes. Two species of fish, hunting as a team.

description:
A fish does a headstand to point at its dinner.
Coral groupers recruit giant moray eels with a head shake, then point out hidden prey.
Would you have guessed a fish could do this?
